title: Tickeron AI flagged $CAPR when an FDA nomination got pulled. It spiked8.8%, then closed red. Is a binary FDA date four days out something anAI model should trade at all?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Today (Wed, Nov 18) Tickeron AI flagged an unusual cluster move in  
biotechs waiting on FDA decisions, and Capricor (CAPR,  
[https://tickeron.com/ticker/CAPR/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/CAPR/)) was near the top of the list.  
  
The trigger wasn't company news. The White House withdrew Dr. Heidi  
Overton's nomination to lead the FDA, and names with pending agency  
decisions caught a bid together. Tickeron AI picked up peers moving  
the same way, including RGNX ([https://tickeron.com/ticker/RGNX/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RGNX/)) and  
REPL ([https://tickeron.com/ticker/REPL/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/REPL/)), which pointed to sector-wide  
regulatory sentiment rather than anything specific to Capricor.  
  
CAPR ran +8.8% to $9.15 by midday, off yesterday's $8.41 close. That  
bounce came after a three-session slide of roughly 25%, from $11.22 on  
Nov 11 to $8.41 on Nov 17.  
  
Then it faded. CAPR closed today at $8.03, down 4.5% on the day.  
  
The real event is this Saturday, Nov 22: the FDA's target action date  
for deramiocel, Capricor's cell therapy for Duchenne muscular  
dystrophy. Options are pricing an outsized move, and label breadth is  
the big unknown.  
  
Full breakdown:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-capricor-therapeutics-capr-stock-up-8-80-today-40565/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-capricor-therapeutics-capr-stock-up-8-80-today-40565/)  
  
Question for the AI traders here: when a model flags a  
sentiment-driven spike right before a binary FDA event, do you let it  
trade the run-up, sit out until the decision, or treat the intraday  
fade as the real signal?
